My land is 6 mu total. I grow wheat in the winter and maize in the summer on the same plots — that's how we've always done it here in Quzhou. Been doing this rotation for over 20 years. My sons help out when needed but they mostly work in the city now, so I need to keep things manageable.

**Wheat (planting around October):**
I'll plant all 6 mu. I'll buy improved seed from the township supply co-op — Jimai or something similar that the neighbors are using. Hybrids are too expensive for wheat and not worth it. I'll do rotary tillage after I clear the maize stalks in late September, break up the soil like I always do. I put down base fertilizer before planting — compound fertilizer plus some urea — and then top-dress with urea in spring around jointing. I pump from the well three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once around heading. I spray herbicide in fall when weeds come up, and spray for aphids and powdery mildew in spring. I expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe a bit more if rain is good.

**Maize (planting right after wheat harvest in June):**
I'll plant straight into the stubble — no need to till again, saves me diesel and labor. Hybrid seed, I'll get Xianyu 335 or Zhengdan 958, whichever the co-op has that's cheaper. Maize needs more fertilizer than wheat. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress with urea at the big bell stage. Summer usually brings rain so I only need to pump maybe twice — once if the seedlings look dry, once if silking hits a dry spell. I spray once for corn borer around that time too. Yield should be around 550 jin per mu.

I'm not changing anything big this year. What I've been doing works well enough and my family doesn't need me to take risks.
